Below is a **complete, minimal‑but‑working** Rust project that

1. Reads the current clipboard text (Windows, macOS, Linux).
2. Sends that text to the ElevenLabs Text‑to‑Speech API.
3. Streams the returned MP3/OGG audio straight to your speakers.

> **TL;DR**  
> ```bash
> cargo new elevenlabs_clipboard_tts
> cd elevenlabs_clipboard_tts
> # copy the Cargo.toml and src/main.rs shown below
> export ELEVENLABS_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
> export ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID="YOUR_VOICE_ID"   # optional – defaults to a free voice
> cargo run
> ```

---

## 1. Project layout

```
elevenlabs_clipboard_tts/
├─ Cargo.toml
└─ src/
   └─ main.rs
```

---

## 2. `Cargo.toml`

```toml
[package]
name = "elevenlabs_clipboard_tts"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

# Optional: enable the `clipboard` feature on Windows only
# (the default `arboard` crate works on all platforms)
[dependencies]
tokio = { version = "1.36", features = ["full"] }
reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["json", "stream"] }
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0"
rodio = "0.17"
arboard = "3.4"          # cross‑platform clipboard
anyhow = "1.0"           # nicer error handling
dotenvy = "0.15"         # load .env files (optional)
```

> **Why these crates?**  
> * `tokio` – async runtime (required by `reqwest`).  
> * `reqwest` – HTTP client.  
> * `serde`/`serde

## 1.  What you’ll need

| Item | Typical part | Why it’s needed |
|------|--------------|-----------------|
| **Microcontroller** | Arduino Uno (or any 5 V AVR board) | Handles the sensor, potentiometer, and LCD |
| **Temperature sensor** | LM35 (analog) or DS18B20 (digital) | Gives you a temperature reading |
| **LCD** | 16×2 character LCD with I²C backpack (or parallel) | Displays the temperature and any other data |
| **Potentiometer** | 10 kΩ (or 5 kΩ) | Lets you adjust a parameter (e.g., back‑light brightness, temperature threshold) |
| **Resistors** | 10 kΩ (for pull‑up on DS18B20) | Needed for proper operation |
